lessons.title: Python Fundamentals
lessons.outcome: Read files, transform records and write small reliable scripts.
lessons.core: Variables and types; lists and dictionaries; conditions and loops; functions and return values; exceptions; pathlib; CSV and JSON; virtual environments.
lessons.build: Write a script that reads orders.csv, rejects invalid rows, calculates revenue by category and exports a summary.csv. Split parsing, validation and reporting into functions.
lessons.verify: Run it twice with different inputs. Test an empty file, a missing column and a malformed price. Add at least four pytest tests.
lessons.interview: Why use a dictionary rather than a list? Explain a KeyError and how it should be handled.

lessons.title: SQL Fundamentals
lessons.outcome: Answer business questions directly from relational tables.
lessons.core: SELECT and WHERE; ORDER BY and LIMIT; COUNT, SUM and AVG; GROUP BY and HAVING; INNER and LEFT JOIN; NULL and COALESCE; basic subqueries.
lessons.build: Create customers and orders tables. Find monthly revenue, top customers, customers without orders and orders with missing customer references.
lessons.verify: Write each query without copying. Compare row counts before and after a JOIN. Explain why a LEFT JOIN may produce NULL.
lessons.interview: Explain WHERE versus HAVING, INNER versus LEFT JOIN and COUNT(*) versus COUNT(column).

lessons.title: Excel
lessons.outcome: Clean, reconcile and explain small business datasets quickly.
lessons.core: Excel tables and filters; relative and absolute references; SUMIFS and COUNTIFS; IF and IFERROR; XLOOKUP; pivot tables; simple charts.
lessons.build: Build a sales workbook with raw data, a lookup sheet, a pivot report and a chart showing monthly sales by region.
lessons.verify: Insert new rows and confirm calculations update. Reconcile pivot totals with source totals and document mismatches.
lessons.interview: When would XLOOKUP, SUMIFS or a pivot table be the best choice?

lessons.title: Git & GitHub
lessons.outcome: Work safely with code changes and communicate a project clearly.
lessons.core: git status/add/commit; branches; pull requests; merge conflicts; .gitignore; README; reproducible setup; issues.
lessons.build: Create a repository for the sales analysis, use a feature branch, make focused commits and open a pull request describing the change.
lessons.verify: Clone into a fresh folder and follow the README. Confirm secrets, local databases and temporary files are excluded.
lessons.interview: Explain how to recover from a bad commit and why a pull request is useful.

lessons.title: Python for Data Analysis
lessons.outcome: Explore and transform data reproducibly with pandas.
lessons.core: read_csv/read_excel; DataFrame selection; filtering; assign; groupby; merge; datetime parsing; NumPy basics; exporting.
lessons.build: Load two datasets, join them, calculate weekly KPIs and produce a tidy analysis table.
lessons.verify: Check data types, merge cardinality and row counts. Recreate the final result from a fresh environment.
lessons.interview: Explain the difference between merge and concat and why chained assignment is risky.

lessons.title: Data Cleaning
lessons.outcome: Make raw data trustworthy without silently hiding problems.
lessons.core: Missingness; duplicates; inconsistent categories; numeric and date types; outliers; validation rules; cleaning logs.
lessons.build: Clean a deliberately messy orders file. Preserve raw input and produce clean data plus a rejected-rows report.
lessons.verify: Write before/after counts and tests for duplicates, null IDs, negative values and impossible dates.
lessons.interview: When should missing values be imputed, dropped or flagged?

lessons.title: Intermediate SQL
lessons.outcome: Write analytical queries used in reporting and interviews.
lessons.core: CTEs; CASE; window functions; ROW_NUMBER; RANK; LAG; date grouping; conditional aggregation; query plans.
lessons.build: Calculate month-over-month growth, each customer's latest order and a rolling revenue metric.
lessons.verify: Verify results on a tiny hand-calculated dataset. Compare window output to GROUP BY output.
lessons.interview: Explain partitioning, window functions versus aggregation and how to find duplicates.

lessons.title: Data Visualization
lessons.outcome: Choose charts that support decisions rather than decoration.
lessons.core: Chart choice; distributions; comparisons; time series; axis integrity; labels; accessible colors; one-sentence insights.
lessons.build: Create three charts for revenue trend, regional performance and order delays, each with a decision-oriented caption.
lessons.verify: Remove unnecessary styling. Check units, zero baselines where relevant and whether the conclusion follows from the data.
lessons.interview: Why is a line chart preferable for trends and when can a dual axis mislead?

lessons.title: Power BI
lessons.outcome: Build a maintainable reporting model and interactive dashboard.
lessons.core: Power Query transformations; star schema relationships; measures versus calculated columns; DAX CALCULATE, DIVIDE and filter context; slicers; refresh.
lessons.build: Build a sales dashboard with KPI cards, trend chart, region filters and drill-through using a fact table and dimensions.
lessons.verify: Reconcile DAX totals with SQL. Test slicers, blank values and refresh. Publish screenshots and a model diagram.
lessons.interview: Explain filter context, one-to-many relationships and why measures are preferred for dynamic KPIs.

lessons.title: Relational Databases
lessons.outcome: Design tables that preserve data integrity and support queries.
lessons.core: Primary and foreign keys; normalization; constraints; indexes; transactions; PostgreSQL basics; EXPLAIN.
lessons.build: Model customers, products, orders and order_items in PostgreSQL with realistic constraints and sample data.
lessons.verify: Try duplicate IDs, orphaned references and transaction rollback. Inspect a query plan before adding an index.
lessons.interview: Explain normalization, indexes and the purpose of transactions.

lessons.title: ETL / ELT
lessons.outcome: Move data from sources to dependable reporting tables.
lessons.core: Extract/transform/load versus extract/load/transform; staging; idempotency; incremental loads; scheduling; logging; retries.
lessons.build: Build a repeatable Python pipeline from CSV or API into PostgreSQL staging and reporting tables.
lessons.verify: Run the pipeline twice without duplicates. Simulate a failed run and demonstrate safe recovery.
lessons.interview: Explain idempotency, incremental loads and when ELT is preferable.

lessons.title: APIs & JSON
lessons.outcome: Collect external data safely and predictably.
lessons.core: HTTP GET and status codes; requests; JSON parsing; pagination; rate limits; timeouts; authentication concepts; secrets via environment variables.
lessons.build: Ingest a paginated public API or local mock API and save normalized records to PostgreSQL.
lessons.verify: Mock 429, 500 and timeout responses. Verify pagination termination and never commit tokens.
lessons.interview: Explain 401 versus 403, pagination and retry with backoff.

lessons.title: Data Quality Testing
lessons.outcome: Detect broken data before it reaches a dashboard.
lessons.core: Schema checks; null and uniqueness rules; referential integrity; accepted ranges; freshness; reconciliation; pytest.
lessons.build: Add automated checks to the ETL pipeline and write a machine-readable validation report.
lessons.verify: Inject bad rows deliberately and confirm failures identify the offending rule. Stop downstream publishing on critical errors.
lessons.interview: Explain what makes a useful data-quality assertion and how false positives are handled.

lessons.title: Data Modeling
lessons.outcome: Organize analytical data around business questions.
lessons.core: Grain; facts and dimensions; star schema; surrogate keys; slowly changing dimensions overview; metric definitions.
lessons.build: Design a sales fact table with date, customer and product dimensions. Document the grain and revenue definition.
lessons.verify: Check that joins do not multiply measures. Compare totals to raw transactions.
lessons.interview: What is table grain and why can a many-to-many join inflate revenue?

lessons.title: Cloud Fundamentals
lessons.outcome: Understand the cloud services used by junior data teams.
lessons.core: AWS S3 objects and buckets; IAM least privilege; managed databases; environment variables; cost awareness; basic monitoring.
lessons.build: Document how a local pipeline would store raw files in S3 and processed data in a managed database. Optionally deploy to a sandbox.
lessons.verify: Explain permissions, data flow and cost controls. Do not put access keys in the repository.
lessons.interview: Describe least privilege, object storage versus a database and how secrets are managed.

lessons.title: Power Automate
lessons.outcome: Automate repeatable business steps with visible controls.
lessons.core: Triggers; actions; conditions; approvals; connectors; error branches; retries; run history.
lessons.build: Design an approval flow: incoming request, validation, manager approval, notification and status update.
lessons.verify: Test approved, rejected, duplicate and failed cases. Capture the flow diagram and run evidence.
lessons.interview: When should a human approval be required and how is a failed run investigated?

lessons.title: Power Apps
lessons.outcome: Create a simple front end for structured business workflows.
lessons.core: Canvas app basics; forms; data sources; validation; role-aware views; Power Automate integration.
lessons.build: Prototype a request form and status screen backed by a simple data table.
lessons.verify: Validate required fields and show what a user can and cannot edit. Document permissions.
lessons.interview: When is a Power App preferable to a custom web application?

lessons.title: UiPath Basics
lessons.outcome: Recognize where robotic process automation helps and where it breaks.
lessons.core: Selectors; attended versus unattended automation; variables; exception handling; logging; brittle UI dependencies.
lessons.build: Map a repetitive spreadsheet-to-form workflow and implement a small safe prototype if UiPath is available.
lessons.verify: Change a form field or input format and observe failure handling. Compare RPA to an API-based alternative.
lessons.interview: Why is API integration usually more robust than screen clicking?

lessons.title: AI Fundamentals
lessons.outcome: Evaluate what an LLM can and cannot safely do in a workflow.
lessons.core: Tokens and context; prompting; structured output; hallucinations; deterministic rules versus LLMs; evaluation sets; cost and latency.
lessons.build: Create a small classification or extraction task with 20 labeled examples. Compare rule-based and LLM outputs if a model is available.
lessons.verify: Record accuracy, failures and cost. Keep a non-LLM fallback for unavailable services.
lessons.interview: When is an LLM justified and how is output validated?

lessons.title: RAG
lessons.outcome: Retrieve supporting documents before generating answers.
lessons.core: Ingestion; chunking; embeddings versus keyword search; retrieval; citations; relevance; evaluation; access boundaries.
lessons.build: Build a document search endpoint returning source passages. Add optional answer generation only when sources support it.
lessons.verify: Use 15 answerable and unanswerable questions. Check citations and require an abstention for unsupported answers.
lessons.interview: How is RAG different from fine-tuning and what causes poor retrieval?

lessons.title: AI Governance
lessons.outcome: Build safeguards into AI-assisted business processes.
lessons.core: Data minimization; access control; PII; audit trails; human review; prompt injection; retention; evaluation records.
lessons.build: Write a threat and control checklist for the automation project, then implement permission checks and audit events.
lessons.verify: Try unauthorized requests and hostile document instructions. Verify no secrets or private data enter logs.
lessons.interview: Explain how human oversight, auditability and source trust reduce risk.

lessons.title: Python Coding Interviews
lessons.outcome: Solve common junior-level tasks clearly under constraints.
lessons.core: Strings and lists; dictionaries and sets; counting; two pointers; sorting; simple complexity; edge cases.
lessons.build: Solve 12 small problems such as deduplication, frequency counting, grouping and CSV aggregation. Explain before coding.
lessons.verify: For each problem state inputs, edge cases, time complexity and at least two tests. Redo missed problems later.
lessons.interview: Explain why a hash map changes the complexity of a repeated lookup.

lessons.title: SQL Interview Exercises
lessons.outcome: Translate ambiguous questions into correct SQL.
lessons.core: Join cardinality; aggregations; NULL; CTEs; window functions; date filtering; deduplication.
lessons.build: Solve 15 realistic questions on orders, customers and transactions without looking at saved solutions.
lessons.verify: Run each query on seed data with known answers. Explain why each JOIN and grouping key is necessary.
lessons.interview: Write a query for second-highest revenue per region and explain tie handling.

lessons.title: Data Case Studies
lessons.outcome: Turn a vague business problem into a measurable analysis.
lessons.core: Clarifying questions; KPI definition; data limitations; segmentation; root-cause analysis; recommendations.
lessons.build: Investigate a simulated decline in order conversion. Define metrics, analyze segments and propose two actions.
lessons.verify: Separate observation from causation. Present assumptions and one follow-up experiment.
lessons.interview: What would be checked before concluding that a campaign caused a decline?

lessons.title: Project Explanation
lessons.outcome: Defend implementation choices with evidence.
lessons.core: Problem, users, architecture, alternatives, validation, failures, limitations and next steps.
lessons.build: Prepare a five-minute walkthrough for each of the three projects with a diagram and live demonstration.
lessons.verify: Answer follow-up questions without notes. Reproduce a test failure and explain the fix.
lessons.interview: Why was this database, model or tool selected instead of an alternative?

lessons.title: Business Communication
lessons.outcome: Report technical work in plain English.
lessons.core: Concise status updates; issue summaries; stakeholder questions; meeting notes; actionable recommendations.
lessons.build: Write a one-page dashboard summary and a short incident update with impact, action, owner and next step.
lessons.verify: Have someone unfamiliar with the project explain the message back. Remove jargon and unsupported claims.
lessons.interview: Explain a failed pipeline to a nontechnical manager in 60 seconds.

lessons.title: German for Work
lessons.outcome: Handle basic workplace exchanges while using English for technical work.
lessons.core: Greetings; scheduling; clarification requests; polite emails; ticket vocabulary; numbers and dates; asking for repetition.
lessons.build: Prepare short German messages for arranging a meeting, reporting a delay and asking a colleague for clarification.
lessons.verify: Practice aloud and check meaning. Keep phrases simple and accurate rather than claiming fluency.
lessons.interview: Give a short introduction and politely request clarification in German.

projects.title: Business Analytics & BI Project
projects.name: Sales & Operations Performance Dashboard
projects.brief: Use synthetic retail transactions, product and region tables. Clean the source, define KPIs, model a star schema and build an interactive Power BI dashboard.
projects.deliver: SQL queries, data dictionary, Power Query transformations, DAX measures, dashboard screenshots, README and a short business recommendation.
projects.accept: Totals reconcile with SQL; filters work; missing and duplicate records are addressed; three decisions can be explained.

projects.title: Data Engineering & Quality Project
projects.name: Reliable Orders Data Pipeline
projects.brief: Ingest CSV plus a paginated mock API into PostgreSQL. Add staging, transformations, incremental loading, data-quality checks and a reporting table.
projects.deliver: Python source, SQL schema, tests, sample synthetic data, run instructions, pipeline diagram, validation report and failure logs.
projects.accept: Second run creates no duplicates; bad input is detected; simulated API failures recover or fail clearly; a fresh clone can reproduce results.

projects.title: Business Automation & AI Project
projects.name: Request Approval & Document Assistant
projects.brief: Build a small request-management application with an API, role-based approval steps, audit history and optional document retrieval. LLM features are optional and must be evaluated separately.
projects.deliver: FastAPI app, database schema, basic UI or API examples, approval workflow, permission tests, audit logs, optional cited retrieval and setup guide.
projects.accept: Unauthorized actions are blocked; every decision is logged; failed operations are handled; retrieval never invents sources.
